explanation: A function call convention defines how arguments are passed to a function and how the return value is retrieved.  Understanding this is crucial for interfacing between different parts of a program, especially when dealing with assembly language programming and understanding how the compiler and hardware interact.  Different architectures and compilers have varying conventions influencing performance and code compatibility.

extraction_metadata.source: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)

book: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)
code_example:
; x86-64 Function Call Convention (SysV ABI)

; 1. Argument Passing (Order 1 through 6)
; Arg1
%rdi
; Arg2
%rsi
; Arg3
%rdx
; Arg4
%rcx
; Arg5
%r8
; Arg6
%r9

; 2. Stack Arguments
; Args 7+ are pushed onto the stack (RSP+0, RSP+8, etc.)

; 3. Return Value
Return (Scalar/Ptr): %rax
Return (Second 64-bit part): %rdx

; 4. Stack Pointer
Stack Pointer: %rsp

; 5. Frame Pointer (Optional)
Frame Pointer: %rbp
keywords: Calling Convention, x86-64 ABI, System V ABI, Argument passing
